issues.legal_issue: A sovereign ruler’s delegation of all authority for administering the state, including authority to make regulations, empowers the delegate to enact legislation within that authority.
material_facts: The ruler possessed executive, legislative, and judicial authority without constitutional limitations.
The ruler delegated all authority for administering the state to the military governor and expressly clarified that the delegation included authority to make regulations.
After the military governor’s appointment ended, the ruler transferred the same administrative powers to the chief minister, who promulgated the commutation regulation.
issues.conclusion: The military governor and the chief minister had legislative authority to promulgate the respective regulations, and the regulations were not invalid for want of legislative competence.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the Farmans according to their terms and held that delegating all authority for administering the state encompassed legislative authority. The Nizam’s sovereignty was not extinguished, but the record showed no withdrawal of the military governor’s authority before the Abolition Regulation or any inconsistent order; the chief minister was given the same authority. The authority to resume jagirs and extinguish interests could therefore be exercised by the delegates.

predicates.appeal_challenges_regulations: The proceeding is an appeal challenging regulations enacted by a delegate of a sovereign ruler.
predicates.sovereign_delegated_all_administrative_a: A sovereign ruler delegated all authority for administering the state to the official who enacted the regulation.
predicates.delegation_included_regulation_power: The delegation expressly or by its terms included authority to make regulations.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges regulations and the sovereign delegated all administrative authority, including regulation-making power, the regulations are within the delegate’s legislative competence.

issues.legal_issue: The doctrine of colourable legislation does not invalidate legislation enacted under unrestricted legislative authority, and no unstated restriction on that authority is inferred without supporting evidence.
material_facts: The ruler had unrestricted sovereign authority and delegated that authority to the military governor, retaining the ability to revoke it or issue inconsistent orders.
There was no evidence that the military governor’s authority had been withdrawn or that an inconsistent order had been issued before the Abolition Regulation.
The chief minister received the same authority when appointed, and the regulations were challenged as confiscatory and as a colourable exercise of legislative power.
issues.conclusion: The regulations could not be invalidated as a colourable exercise of legislative authority, and the claimed restriction on the delegated power was not established.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of colourable legislation applies where a legislature is subject to constitutional restrictions and uses a statute to evade them. It does not apply to legislation enacted by an authority whose powers are not fettered by constitutional or other limitations. The court found no basis to infer an implied restriction on the sovereign’s delegation.

predicates.appeal_challenges_regulations: The proceeding is an appeal challenging regulations enacted under delegated legislative authority.
predicates.colourable_exercise_alleged: The challenger alleges that the regulation is a colourable exercise of legislative power.
predicates.delegated_legislative_authority_unrestri: The delegated legislative authority was not subject to constitutional or other limitations.

issues.definition: An appeal alleging colourable legislation fails when it challenges regulations enacted under delegated legislative authority that was unrestricted.

issues.legal_issue: Pre-Constitution legislation that had already extinguished rights does not revive those rights on the Constitution’s commencement, and legislation included in the Ninth Schedule is protected from a challenge based on inconsistency with Part III.
material_facts: The Abolition Regulation and the Commutation Regulation were enacted before the Constitution commenced.
The Abolition Regulation had extinguished the jagirdar’s rights in the jagir, and the Commutation Regulation had determined the commutation payable before the Constitution commenced.
Both regulations were later included in the Ninth Schedule by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act.
issues.conclusion: The appellant had no rights in the jagirs at the commencement of the Constitution and could not obtain restoration of possession or commutation outside the regulation; the regulations were also exempt from challenge on the ground that they violated Part III rights.
issues.legal_principle: The Constitution does not operate retrospectively, and rights extinguished by legislation before its commencement are not thereby revived, as held in Keshavan Madhava Menon v. State of Bombay, [1951] S.C.R. 228. Article 31B protects laws included in the Ninth Schedule from being deemed void on the ground that they are inconsistent with, take away, or abridge rights in Part III.

predicates.appeal_challenges_preconstitution_regula: The proceeding is an appeal challenging regulations enacted before the Constitution commenced.
predicates.regulations_were_preconstitution: The challenged regulations were enacted before the Constitution commenced.
predicates.rights_extinguished_before_constitution: The challenged legislation had extinguished the claimant’s relevant rights before the Constitution commenced.
predicates.regulations_in_ninth_schedule: The challenged regulations were included in the Ninth Schedule.
predicates.fundamental_rights_challenge_and_revival: A challenge based on Part III rights and a claim to revive rights already extinguished are unavailable.

issues.definition: A challenge and revival claim fail when a pre-Constitution regulation had already extinguished the relevant rights or the regulation is included in the Ninth Schedule.
